notes:
Summary: Mid-market SaaS (knowledge management) building semantic search over customer docs and in-product recommendations. Primary initiative: migrate embedding generation and semantic ranking off a hosted managed provider to Redwood Hosted initially with clear path to Dedicated/reserved capacity for predictable batch windows and cost reduction.

Key stakeholders: CTO (Ravi Menon) — cares about latency and data residency; Head of ML (Sophie Nguyen) — cares about embedding quality and offline batch cost; Infrastructure Lead (Diego Ramos) — concerned about vector DB connectors and network egress.

What they told us / call snippets:
- "Need to get nightly embedding runs off our EC2 fleet — costs are spiking during peak indexing weeks" (Sophie)
- "If Redwood can guarantee steady throughput for reserved windows and easy connector to Pinecone, we can consider a 12-month commit" (Ravi)

Technical notes / obs from SE calls:
- Current stack: extractor -> local preprocessing -> calls to third-party embedding API -> store vectors in Pinecone; nightly batch is ~120k docs (avg length 1.3k tokens) -> currently takes 14 hours and expensive (egress and per-token costs).
- They measured a trial on Hosted: 40ms/sample at small batch sizes but saw throughput drop when parallelizing to 200 concurrent workers (rate limit fallback behavior). Needs evaluation of Redwood continuous batching & autoscaling.
- Must support SSE/KMS integration for key lifecycle and audit logs for HIPAA-like customers; legal asked for data residency statement for EU customers (they have EU tenants).

POC scope notes (agreed):
- Set up Dedicated pool for 2 weeks in us-east and run full nightly pipeline twice. Measure cost, total time, and tail latencies. Compare against baseline (current provider).
- Integrate Redwood connectors to write embeddings to Pinecone; validate vector format, distance metric, and metadata passthrough.
- Run reranking experiments (hybrid search + semantic) with Redwood Optimize suggestions for quantization and batching.

Risks & open questions:
- Vector DB write throughput: Pinecone throughput limits might become the bottleneck; consider writing to S3 + ingest path or recommend Milvus for bulk load.
- Legal data residency: they require EU customer embeddings to be processed in eu-west region; need formal statement and SLA.
- Cost model: finance needs an ARR-linked pricing example for reserved capacity vs on-demand hosting.

Next steps (short):
- Redwood to enable a Dedicated trial window and provide an initial reserved capacity pricing sheet (Aisha) — due 2026-03-12.
- SE to prepare connector runbook for Pinecone and parallel ingestion patterns (Liam) — due 2026-03-13.
- Customer legal to provide list of data residency requirements and contract redlines.
